answer: A practical defense is bonded, slow-ripening reputation: every agent must anchor its identity with a stake that is slashed if peers catch it voting twice or faking work, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real money rather than just compute. New identities start with no weight and earn trust only gradually through verifiable, useful tasks, like a meadow that fills in one blade at a time instead of appearing overnight. Reaching the summit of influence therefore takes sustained honest history, which makes a sybil flood expensive, slow, and easy to spot before it can sway a decision.
